title: About AI generated content on a game

posts.author: SutoriTheRat
posts.body:
Hi, I wanted to clarify the use of AI on certain areas of a game, Since one of the plugins I use was made by an automated scripting tool, the plugin itself doesn't contribute to the overall gameplay, it's function is to allow me to place my own images on the black borders of the full screen mode (For example, what Undertale does in its console version)
Therefore, if needed, I can remove it without any problems if the rules require it.
My question is, could using this plugin affect the game's future release in any way? Since I wanted to publish the game on this forum first.
I'd like to clarify this to avoid any problems later on.
I understand that the rules prohibit publishing AI-generated content for distribution, such as images, music, or individual plugins, and this plugin is not a free resource and it's not intended to be distributed or used by any other creator.
(I will not attach the plugin content for obvious reasons, if it's necessary for clarification, then it will be shared through the thread dedicated to uploading AI content)

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
SutoriTheRat said:
My question is, could using this plugin affect the game's future release in any way? Since I wanted to publish the game on this forum first.
Click to expand...
Yes. Itch.io as well as steam require you to disclose any and all use of AI tools. Therefore, people who wish to not support such practices will likely avoid the game and potentially future games as well.
As for the forums: Games that use AI tools are allowed to have threads, but also require the same type of disclosure, resulting in the same behavior as stated above for likely most people on here.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
TLDR;
Based on your scenario, yes, you need a disclaimer about AI use in posting your game on this forum, but you wouldn't be restricted from posting the game here. You also have options if that bothers you and you don't want to use such a disclaimer.
Long response. Don't read if you don't care.
Personally, I wouldn't be overly concerned about needing to use an AI content disclaimer in a non-commercial game. The real issue is what was AI used for in the game. And I certainly wouldn't stress about it until the game was actually finished and ready for release.
If anyone wants to completely disregard your game the minute they see the disclaimer, without actually reading what AI was used for, well, that's their personal choice. But I wouldn't make the mistake of believing that would be the overwhelming standard response.
If the plugin isn't really needed, then I would seriously consider just removing it if having to put the AI disclaimer on the game really bothers you.
If you really want what the plugin provides for your release AND your game is pretty much ready for release, then I would seriously consider trying to get assistance with a non-AI generated version of the plugin if having the disclaimer really bothers you.
You could also proactively find a replacement that has already been made, such as referenced in the previous response.
You could also consider working towards learning how to make your own plugin without the AI assistance. But that might be very difficult depending on how complex the plugin actually is.
Finally, I don't intend to use any AI asset (audio, visual, plugin) in my Sudoku game out of respect for those on this forum who have helped me with questions and whose assets I am using.
HOWEVER, I still plan on putting an AI disclaimer on my game and crediting Google AI mode (out of a sheer abundance of caution) because I am using AI more and more for researching how to do things with Javascript. I'm not just blindly having AI write Javascript code for me that I copy and paste and indiscriminately use.
Instead, I ask Google AI mode how I would do something using Javascript (sometimes how I would use Javascript specifically for RPG Maker MZ) I use any proposed AI code as part of my research into how to use Javascript. I read it for understanding, ask for clarification of parts I don't completely understand, I reference the W3Schools online course and a book I am learning from to better understand the concepts, and I experiment with and test my understanding of the pieces of the code.
But I think it would be disingenuous to pretend that I didn't have AI assistance in the learning process. And if any part of any script remains unchanged from what was proposed by Google AI then I believe that falls under the current description of what requires the AI disclaimer. I don't personally agree with that, but I don't write the rules, I just have to interpret them the best way that I can.
Not my circus, not my monkeys.
To me, there isn't any difference in learning and working from Javascript that AI helped generate than there is in learning and working from Javascript that I found posted somewhere else on a forum, or in a tutorial, or in a book, etc. For me, using the AI search to find multiple proposed consolidated solutions is just 1,000 times faster and has exponentially increased the speed of my learning and understanding Javascript concepts. Google AI helps me refine what I'm trying to do and what I'm trying to research.
So, for me, if being honest about using Google AI mode to assist with some of the Javascript makes some people just completely skip over my free game or makes them unhappy with me, I'm ok with that. But that is a personal choice and I prefer to be honest instead of pretending that AI didn't help in any way.
But if I'm going to credit other forum users who have helped me with code examples, I feel it is only appropriate to also list other sources, like Google AI.
I don't think that an AI disclaimer is the veritable kiss of death for a game and I think it depends significantly on what the AI was used for.
And again, I really wouldn't worry about it until the game was completed. Then, when faced with the final decision, based on the landscape at that time, you could easily look for alternatives. Like making a post that you essentially have a completed game that you want to release but there is one plugin that was created with AI assistance and you would really like some human assistance in replacing it. It is very possible that you could get someone willing to help with that. Or getting help finding an existing plugin that already does what you need.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
SutoriTheRat said:
the use of AI on certain areas
Click to expand...
A lot of the problems some people have with AI (unless they are just repeating what they read elsewhere without intelligence of their own) should become more clear once you stop and think about how any and all AIs work. Because there is no intelligence in any computer at all, we (as entire mankind) simply aren't there technologically.
An AI has a large database of tagged examples. These examples were all done by humans, no exceptions to that (if you're re-using AI products, some times they started with human examples).
Then someone "trained" the AI by placing tags of keywords on those examples (and/or parts of the examples).
Now on using the AI, once you give it some keywords it searches its database for the same keywords and randomly puts the examples tagged with those keywords together.
That is usually followed by a consistency check, in the case of code with syntax and/or grammar routines to make the result look "nice". In the case of pictures those consistency checks still have problems, which is why you're still getting humans with six or more fingers sometimes.
And with code it usually does not do what it is supposed to do unless you were lucky and someone had done the same before and had it correctly tagged in the examples.
Using an AI to search for something that you will use yourself (especially about code) is no problem at all and has been done even before the internet using books and reference catalogues.
But using an AI to get a "finished" product means that you're using some unknown humans work without knowing if said human allowed their work to be used that way.
And that last is what people have problems with, similar to using ripped resources or any other form of copyright theft.
